title: Traffic Oscillator KPI & Fallback Playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick operational playbook for small-to-medium launch windows where traffic is expected to oscillate (spikes + drops) across regions. Combines a compact KPI scorecard, triage play, and fallback routing heuristics so oncall/product-ops can make fast decisions without hunting for multiple docs.

TL;DR:
- Run the KPI fast-check each 10m during first 72h post-launch.
- If latency P95 > target AND error-rate > 2x baseline for 2 consecutive 10m buckets, trigger tier-1 fallback (route 20% traffic to fallback model).
- If cost-per-1000 tokens > budget threshold and latency OK, consider surge-quantization (reduce max_tokens by 20%).

1) KPI Scorecard (compact, for 10m cadence) — fields to read in order of priority:
- traffic_in_rps: observed requests/sec (int)
- success_rate: 200s / total requests (pct) -> baseline target >= 99.5%
- p95_latency_ms: target < 350ms for hosted API; < 150ms for dedicated lanes
- avg_tokens_per_request: used for cost projection
- errors_5xx_rate: baseline <= 0.2%
- model_confidence_regressions: number of prompts failing golden set (count)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: rolling 1h estimate

Quick interpretation guide:
- Green: success_rate >= 99.5% AND p95_latency within target
- Amber: success_rate 98–99.5% OR p95_latency 1.2x target
- Red: success_rate < 98% OR p95_latency > 1.5x target OR errors_5xx_rate > 0.5%

2) Roadmap lanes (short-term milestones to run during rollout)
- L1: Traffic shaping and routing (owner: Marco Alvarez)
  - M1: Enable canary weights (0% -> 5% -> 20%)
  - M2: Activate regional fallback policies (us-east -> us-west -> eu)
- L2: Model-performance checks (owner: Priya Kapoor)
  - M1: Golden prompts run every 5m against current model and fallback variant
  - M2: Auto-rollback threshold configured (5% quality regressions in 30m)
- L3: Cost controls (owner: Sofia Martinez)
  - M1: Burst-quantization toggle available (manual + policy)
  - M2: Token caps per route enforced via routing policy

3) Immediate oncall checklist (first 72 hours)
- 00:00 — warmup: pre-populate prefix cache for top-100 prompt families (engineering runbook: infra/cache-warmup-2025).
- Continuous: monitor KPI scorecard dashboard every 10m. Use the short checklist below for a red/amber bucket.
- Red bucket steps (execute in order):
  1) Post to #prodops-launch with summary: RPS, p95, 5xx rate, canary weight
  2) Notify SRE and model-oncall via Slack: @sre-oncall @model-oncall
  3) Trigger tier-1 fallback: shift 20% of traffic to fallback-model-v1 (routing API: /routes/traffic-shift).
  4) If no improvement in 30 minutes, escalate to tier-2: shift 60% and open incident.
- Amber bucket steps:
  1) Reduce canary weight back to previous steady-state or throttle non-critical routes
  2) Run quick bisect: disable last deployment(s) + enable golden-run to check regressions

4) Fallback routing heuristics (policy snippets for engineers/operators)
- Use multi-dimensional routing: prioritize by (latency, region, customer-tier).
- Example policy: if region_p95_ms > 1.2x target AND errors_5xx_rate > 0.3% -> route 30% of gold traffic to small-quantized-model in same region.
- Safe-fallback list (approved variants):
  - fallback-small-q4 (lower cost, 95% semantic match for simple prompts)
  - fallback-latency-optimized (reduced context window, faster kernels)
  - fallback-regional-cache (reads cached responses for detected idempotent flows)

5) Capacity & surge play (cost-aware):
- If RPS > forecast * 1.5 for > 15m -> contact infra-team to spin dedicated nodes (Slack: #infra-autoscale-request).
- If cost_per_1k_tokens spikes but latency stable -> toggle burst-quantization for background routes.
- For IO-heavy workloads (high avg_tokens_per_request), cap concurrent requests per API-key to protect KV caches.

6) Signals to avoid immediate rollback (we should prefer routing/fallback over rollback unless clear quality regression):
- Spike caused by synthetic traffic (check internal traffic tagger)
- Large, short-lived client retries (client-side misconfiguration)
- Regional network blips (DNS or cloud region issue)

7) Communication templates (paste to Slack/incidents):
- Launch alert (10m): "LAUNCH ALERT: us-east p95=420ms (target 350), success=98.6%, 5xx=0.6% -> enacted tier-1 fallback (20%). See dashboard: <link>"
- Escalation (30m): "ESCALATION: Tier-2 enacted. Routing 60% to fallback. Incident opened: PRODINC-<id>. Model-oncall pinged."

8) Short-run experiments to run if ambiguous:
- Experiment A: Move 10% traffic to latency-optimized model and measure conversational completion quality on golden set for 30m.
- Experiment B: Reduce max_tokens by 15% on background flows to evaluate cost delta without user-surface impact.

9) Open questions / decisions needed (for product leadership before next launch)
- Define firm SLO thresholds for P95 across dedicated vs hosted tiers (proposal attached in Confluence).
- Approve automatic 20% route shifts for tier-1 fallback without exec signoff.
- Decide acceptable cost-per-1k_tokens ceiling for public betas.

10) Next steps (this doc owner + immediate owners):
- Sofia: finalize cost ceilings and add to routing policies (due 2025-09-19).
- Marco: script one-click route-shift in console (due 2025-09-21).
- Priya: add golden-set health check into alerting pipeline (due 2025-09-20).

Reference links (operational):
- Dashboard (scorecard): Sheet:traffic-oscillator-sim-2025 (linked above)
- Runbook: infra/cache-warmup-2025
- Incident template: /confluence/incidents/launch-template

Notes-to-self (informal):
- When running golden checks, sample across top funnels (text-gen, chat, embeddings). Keep sample size small (50/min) to avoid cost but keep signal.
- Revisit fallback-variant fidelity metrics after first 24h (accuracy + hallucination rates).

End of doc.
